_comment: Every place a fact in this app can come from, and how much it can be trusted. The app shows this next to results, so a reader always knows whether they are looking at something checked by a scholar, worked out by a rule, or guessed by a machine. Adding a source means adding it here, not in code.
_confidence_comment: verified = a person checked it · derived = a fixed rule produced it, same answer every time · translated = the source's own content, put into English by a machine with the original beside it · guessed = a statistical model or an AI produced it and it can be wrong
_field_comment: label/confidence/detail are what a result badge shows. url is the thing itself on the web, empty where there is nothing public to link to, never a guessed address. where is one plain sentence saying where it physically lives, for a reader who does not know what a corpus or a dump is. used_in lists the tabs that read it, and drives the line at the foot of each tab; a source used by no tab is a source nothing reads, which is a bug worth seeing. url may be '@name' or '@name:path', resolved against _links, so a shared address is written once.
_category_comment: category is the shelf a source sits on, in a reader's words: Qur'an, Tafsir, Grammar, Fiqh, and whatever is added next. Daleel's book picker groups by it, and choosing a shelf searches everything on it. Only sources Daleel searches need one; anything without a category is simply never offered as a shelf.

corpus.label: Quranic Arabic Corpus
corpus.detail: Tagged by hand, word by word. Version 0.4, GNU GPL, corpus.quran.com
corpus.where: Every Quranic word hand-tagged. Stored locally.

translation.label: Quran.com
translation.detail: From the Quran.com project: each word glossed on its own, in English and in Urdu, and whole translations of the ayah
translation.where: Word-by-word (English, Urdu) and full translations. Stored locally.

mushaf.label: Madani mushaf layout
mushaf.detail: Page breaks of the 604-page, 15-line Madani printing, from Quran.com
mushaf.where: Page each ayah starts on, 604-page Madani. Stored locally.

tafsir.label: Ibn Kathir (Abridged)
tafsir.detail: A scholar's commentary on the ayah, in English, from Quran.com
tafsir.where: Ibn Kathir, abridged English. Stored locally.

recitation-audio.label: EveryAyah
recitation-audio.detail: Recordings of each ayah by well-known reciters, played from everyayah.com
recitation-audio.where: Ayah audio, fetched on play. Only the ayah number is sent.

qul.label: Quranic Universal Library
qul.detail: Tafsirs and translations, downloaded once from qul.tarteel.ai
qul.where: Tafsirs and translations; each with its own terms. Stored locally.

rules.label: Sarf rule tables
rules.detail: Built from the conjugation patterns in data/sarf/patterns.json, the same answer every time
rules.where: Conjugation tables by fixed rule. Same word, same table.

nahw.label: Nahw rule engine
nahw.detail: Grammar rules applied in order, from data/nahw_rules/rules.json
nahw.where: Grammar rules applied in order. Same sentence, same answer.

tasheel.label: Tasheel al-Nahw
tasheel.detail: Worked examples transcribed by hand from a printed book
tasheel.where: Printed book (Dar al-Sa'adah, 2011). Diagrams hand-typed. No web copy.

tarkeeb.label: Tarkeeb rules
tarkeeb.detail: The corpus's word tags, joined into a bracket tree by rule
tarkeeb.where: Tree from corpus tags by rule, where Treebank has none. Gaps left visible.

wiktionary.label: Wiktionary
wiktionary.detail: Community-written and openly licensed (CC BY-SA). Broad, but thinner than a printed dictionary on rare classical words

maqayees.label: Maqayees al-Lugha (Ibn Faris)
maqayees.detail: The origin sense, up to the entry's first full stop, 4,738 roots
maqayees.where: Ibn Faris (d. 395 AH), 4,738 roots. 98.4% match with a second copy.

maqayees_deck.label: Maqayees: checking copy
maqayees_deck.detail: A second typed copy, used only to check this text
maqayees_deck.where: Second typed copy (4,726 entries). Check only; no text used.

maqayees_english.label: Maqayees: English of the origin sense
maqayees_english.detail: A model's one-line gloss, unproofread, about 1 in 50 wrong
maqayees_english.where: One-line AI gloss, unproofread. ~1 in 50 wrong on 300 checked.

maqayees_translation.label: Maqayees: English of the whole entry
maqayees_translation.detail: The book's own Arabic, put into English by a model, with the Arabic beside it
maqayees_translation.where: Whole entry, AI translated. Arabic shown beside. Unproofread.

ai.label: AI explanation
ai.detail: Written by a language model. Useful for wording, not proof; check it against the rules above
ai.where: Model-written each time. Wording aid, not evidence.

recitation.label: Heard by Groq or this machine
recitation.detail: What a recitation sounded like, written down by Groq online when it answers, otherwise on this computer
recitation.where: Groq Whisper, else local model; matched to Quran text. Nothing kept.

recitation-letters.label: tilawa
recitation-letters.detail: Finds where on the page a recitation is. tilawa v0.2.0 by yazinsai on GitHub (MIT), built on NVIDIA's Arabic FastConformer (CC-BY-4.0)
recitation-letters.where: Local model (MIT). Locates the recited words; never grades them.

nahw-books.label: Classical Nahw & Sarf
nahw-books.detail: Thirty works, from Sibawayh's Kitab and Ibn Jinni's Khasais through Ibn Hisham to Suyuti. Printed page numbers kept; no harakat in these texts.
nahw-books.where: 30 classical works, Sibawayh to Suyuti. Stored locally.

fiqh-books.label: Hanafi Fiqh & Usul
fiqh-books.detail: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Bidayat al-Mubtadi with al-Hidaya, Usul al-Shashi. Printed page numbers kept; no harakat in these texts.
fiqh-books.where: Quduri, Hidaya, Usul al-Shashi. Stored locally.

jazariyya.label: Al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah
jazariyya.detail: All 107 verses with their harakat. The English beside each verse is our own short gloss of what it says, not a translation
jazariyya.where: Ibn al-Jazari's poem, 107 verses, hand-typed from print. Own English gloss.

openiti-lexicons.label: Classical Arabic dictionaries
openiti-lexicons.detail: Lisan al-Arab and Taj al-Arus, whole entries, filed by root
openiti-lexicons.where: Lisan al-Arab, Taj al-Arus, by root. Stored locally.

lane.label: Lane's Arabic-English Lexicon
lane.detail: Edward William Lane, 1863-1893. Arabic explained in English, 5,183 roots
lane.where: Perseus, Tufts (CC BY-SA 3.0). Arabic explained in English.

timelines.label: Timeline notes
timelines.detail: Order and summaries written with Claude; Qur'an references read against the text; hadith numbers checked against sunnah.com
timelines.where: Hand-written notes. Quran refs and hadith numbers checked.

lubab.label: al-Suyuti, Lubab al-Nuqul
lubab.detail: Reports on why an ayah came down, cut out of al-Suyuti's book by rule and matched to their ayahs
lubab.where: Asbab reports cut by rule, matched to ayahs. English by Claude.

colloquial.label: Colloquial lessons
colloquial.detail: Damascene phrases, conversations and exercises written by Claude; no native speaker has checked them yet
colloquial.where: One file per unit in backend/data/colloquial, generated to the prompt in docs/colloquial-authoring-prompt.md. Spoken Arabic is not written down in any corpus this app has, so nothing here was checked against a source: it is a model's account of how Damascus speaks. Pictures beside the phrases come from Openverse and each carries its own creator and licence.

nahw-notes.label: Year 3 Nahw notes
nahw-notes.detail: Your teacher's own notes, read off the page by Claude; the page itself is one tap away
nahw-notes.where: Year 3 teacher's notes, read by Claude. Page cited per block.
